summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: asymptotic analysis (O, Omega, Theta), divide-and-conquer recurrences and standard algorithms including Karatsuba multiplication and the radix-two FFT for polynomial multiplication, and basic models of computation including multitape Turing machines. From discrete mathematics they know induction, sets and binomial coefficients, binary and two's-complement representation, primes, gcd, modular arithmetic and the Chinese remainder theorem. From a first linear algebra course they know vector spaces, bases, subspaces, matrices, invertibility, Gaussian elimination, permutation and diagonal matrices and projections, and from calculus the exponential and logarithm, geometric series, Newton's method and elementary error bounds such as the triangle inequality. They have not studied Fourier analysis beyond the FFT, abstract algebra beyond modular arithmetic, numerical analysis of fixed-point transforms, or research-level integer multiplication techniques such as Schönhage–Strassen, Nussbaumer transforms or Gaussian resampling.

known.name: Big-Omega and Big-Theta notation
known.gloss: f = Ω(g) means f is eventually at least a constant times g, and f = Θ(g) means f is both O(g) and Ω(g).

known.name: Worst-case running time
known.gloss: The maximum number of steps an algorithm takes over all inputs of a given length, as a function of that length.

known.name: Logarithms, floor and ceiling
known.gloss: The logarithm inverts exponentiation, and floor and ceiling round a real number down or up to an integer.

known.name: Exponential function
known.gloss: The function x ↦ e^x, its basic identities and growth, including functions such as exp(−πx²) built from it.

known.name: Euler's formula and complex roots of unity
known.gloss: e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ, so the n-th roots of unity e^{2πik/n} are the n complex numbers with zⁿ = 1, a primitive one generating all of them by its powers.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a sum of digits times powers of a base such as 2 or 2ᵇ, padded with leading zeros to a fixed length.

known.name: Two's complement
known.gloss: The representation of an integer z with −2^{w−1} ≤ z < 2^{w−1} by the w-bit binary form of z mod 2ʷ.

known.name: Fixed-point numbers and rounding
known.gloss: Representing reals as integer multiples of 2⁻ᵖ and approximating a value by truncating or rounding it to that grid, so a value known to within less than 1/2 of an integer rounds to it exactly.

known.name: Integer division with remainder
known.gloss: For integers a and b > 0 there are unique q and 0 ≤ r < b with a = qb + r.

known.name: Prime numbers and trial division
known.gloss: An integer greater than 1 is prime if its only positive divisors are 1 and itself, which can be checked by trying all divisors up to its square root.

known.name: Greatest common divisor and coprimality
known.gloss: The gcd of two integers is the largest integer dividing both, and they are coprime when it equals 1.

known.name: Modular inverses and units
known.gloss: A residue a modulo q has a multiplicative inverse, i.e. is a unit, exactly when gcd(a, q) = 1.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli s₁, …, s_d, the map x ↦ (x mod s₁, …, x mod s_d) is a bijection from ℤ/(s₁⋯s_d) to the product of the ℤ/sᵢ that respects addition and multiplication.

known.name: Fast Fourier transform
known.gloss: The divide-and-conquer algorithm computing a discrete Fourier transform of power-of-two length n in O(n log n) arithmetic operations through log₂ n layers of two-point butterflies, used to multiply polynomials by evaluation, pointwise product and interpolation.

known.name: Polynomial evaluation and interpolation
known.gloss: A polynomial of degree below n is determined by its values at n distinct points, so products can be computed by evaluating, multiplying values and interpolating.

known.name: Karatsuba multiplication
known.gloss: The recursive algorithm multiplying two n-digit numbers with three half-size products instead of four, in O(n^{log₂ 3}) time.

known.name: Divide-and-conquer recurrences
known.gloss: Equations such as T(n) = aT(n/b) + f(n) expressing an algorithm's cost through its subproblems, solved by summing the costs level by level of the recursion tree.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: The sum 1 + a + ⋯ + a^{k} = (a^{k+1} − 1)/(a − 1), which for a > 1 is within a constant factor of its last term and for a < 1 is bounded by 1/(1 − a).

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: Proving a statement for all n by proving it for a base case and showing each case implies the next.

known.name: Sets, Cartesian products and lexicographic order
known.gloss: The Cartesian product of sets is the set of tuples with one entry from each, ordered lexicographically by comparing the first differing entry.

known.name: Subsets and binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The number of k-element subsets of an h-element set is the binomial coefficient h!/(k!(h − k)!).

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: A bijection of a finite set to itself, representable as a matrix with one 1 in each row and column, which reorders the entries of a vector.

known.name: Hamming weight
known.gloss: The number of nonzero coordinates of a bit vector.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces, bases and dimension
known.gloss: A vector space over a field is closed under addition and scalar multiplication, and its dimension is the size of any basis, a linearly independent spanning set.

known.name: Invertible matrices and the general linear group
known.gloss: A square matrix is invertible when some matrix multiplies it to the identity, and the invertible m×m matrices over a field form the group GL(m, F).

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Reducing a matrix by elementary row operations to triangular or echelon form, which computes rank and inverses and factors invertible matrices into elementary and triangular ones.

known.name: Diagonal matrices and pointwise products
known.gloss: A diagonal matrix multiplies each coordinate of a vector by its own scalar, i.e. it is the entrywise product with a fixed vector.

known.name: Linear projections
known.gloss: A linear map P with P² = P, which maps onto a subspace U and is the identity on U, along a complementary subspace that it sends to zero.

known.name: Matrix transpose
known.gloss: The matrix obtained by swapping rows and columns, which for a stored array exchanges its two index coordinates.

known.name: Maximum norm and triangle inequality
known.gloss: The max norm of a vector is the largest absolute value of its entries, and norms satisfy ‖x + y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ + ‖y‖, which lets errors be added along a computation.

known.name: Newton's method
known.gloss: The iteration x ↦ x − f(x)/f′(x) for approximating a root, whose quadratic convergence roughly doubles the number of correct digits each step.

known.name: Depth-first traversal
known.gloss: Visiting a tree or recursion by fully processing each child subtree before moving to the next sibling.
